reuse.why: Routes forecast-schedules, the API model and the server paths through getScheduledAmount and takes the tolerance from the existing getApproxNumberThreshold, but schedule-template.ts writes its own op dispatch over the new range and approx helpers.

duplication.why: Removes the hand-written midpoint copy in forecast-schedules.ts, but schedule-template.ts keeps its own isbetween/isapprox/is dispatch that duplicates the dispatch inside getScheduledAmount.

placement.why: The worst-case rules sit in shared/schedules.ts and expectedAmount is added in the API model's toExternal, both fitting places, while one server consumer still dispatches the rule itself.

scope.why: Focused on the four requests: the amount rule, its callers, the API field and the release notes.

maintainability.why: The operator is an optional trailing argument after the inverse flag, so the desktop callers (Balance, SchedulesTable, the mobile schedules views, useScheduleEdit) silently keep planning approximate amounts at their exact value, and schedule-template has to be kept in step by hand.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList dispatches getRangeWorstCase / getApproxWorstCase itself instead of calling getScheduledAmount with the operator

disguised_duplication.where: schedule-template.ts: the nested op ternary over getRangeWorstCase/getApproxWorstCase restates getScheduledAmount's dispatch in a different shape instead of calling it

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter and an isapprox branch; schedule-template.ts re-implements the dispatch; the desktop-client callers call the helper without op and so never get the approximate rule
